comments.text:
My concern is not that Cenk misspoke. Everyone makes mistakes, especially during live discussions. My concern is that making factual claims without verifying them can cast doubt on other information being presented. The statement that soy sauce is Japanese is a good example because it is an easily verifiable fact—soy sauce originated in China, even though Japan developed its own well-known styles.

I am not suggesting that Cenk was being dishonest. I believe he was simply repeating something he thought was true. However, when easily checked facts turn out to be incorrect, it can affect how people perceive the reliability of statements on subjects that are much more difficult for the average person to verify, such as complex political or current events. Accuracy on small, easily confirmed details helps build confidence in the credibility of larger claims.
